chapter: Early bands, Calloway to Basie and Kansas City (third typescript)
title: Why he preferred sitting in to big-band section work
summary: Sitting in gave him freedom to play his own thing, while in big bands solos were not distributed fairly and arrangers or leaders chose who played.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: When you made this sort of speech -- you made the switch from big bands to small groups -- was that a big change in terms of your own playing, or was it just because you said earlier when we were talking that you just used to sit in a lot just to take your horn around.
So, scratching out a little more might not have been that much of a change although --

Yeah, that's where I'd get my kicks -- was sitting in with guys you know -- because if -- you could play your own thing. And when you get in those big bands you're confined to that music. So you know -- now and then you get a chance to play. You get a chance to let yourself go. You know. Some bands that I've played in -- I guess I wouldn't want to name the names -- but they had good solos then and there was no reason why I should have a bigger solo -- you know -- but they had all the solos.

You know what I mean -- they wasn't distributed around enough I suppose -- you know. So it would be weeks before I'd play any kind of solo because they never would play the beats that my solo was in. (Inaudible).
